findings.trigger: A proxy/upstream trickles response headers more frequently than the 12-second socket timeout during configure/core-update/rollback readiness; the same weakness exists in core download headers/body within the 30-second socket timeout.
findings.impact: Readiness can remain selected while holding management.lock for an unbounded practical duration, delaying commit/compensation and blocking administration. Core downloads similarly exceed their 300-second total budget because elapsed time is checked only after blocking open/header/read returns.

locations: deploy/service_proxy.py:408-414 no total deadline around HTTPSConnection/request/getresponse
deploy/proxy_core.py:167-174 open/read occurs before elapsed budget check

slowHeaders.result: Real local socket/http.client parser accepted progressive headers for 13.547 seconds with timeout=12 and returned ready. HTTPSConnection replaced with HTTPConnection solely to isolate parser timeout semantics; TLS/CONNECT/nft/systemd not tested.

slowBody.result: Real urllib loopback socket delivered 16 bytes over 0.813 actual seconds. At 1000x monotonic time, the 300-second budget was checked only at 813 virtual seconds after read returned. This was accelerated-clock evidence, not an 813-second live test.

evidence.repairBoundary: Total deadline must enclose complete DNS/open/redirect/CONNECT/TLS/request/header/body lifecycle, preserve cleanup/origin/credentials/no-retry behavior, and permit transaction compensation on expiry.

findings.trigger: install_control wrapper has no current call/import; initialize uses initialize_recorded and control update uses stage_control directly.
findings.impact: Unused alternate installation entrypoint adds misleading maintenance surface beside the resumable installation flow.

evidence.references: Current-source rg finds only definition; install.py:155-156 uses initialize_recorded and control_update.py:598 uses stage_control.
evidence.repairBoundary: Remove wrapper; no behavior-mirroring test needed.

findings.trigger: Retain 32 managed worktrees under one execution identity, switch between native and Root while retaining the supervisor home, then create another worktree from a repository owned by the newly selected identity. Its new nativeHome can be below the helper-local limit while the shared supervisor managed_worktrees table is already full.
findings.impact: The helper creates the new checkout before the shared capacity check rejects its positive acknowledgement. The witness transaction rolls back to unknown without a binding, so the new retained checkout cannot be read/attached through the managed worktree API and requires manual inspection. This unnecessarily exceeds the intended shared retention budget and enters activity uncertainty instead of a safe not_sent capacity rejection.
evidence: RuntimeWorkspace executes runWorkspace first (src/runtime/workspace-service.ts:61) and only then witness.complete (line 65). Its beforeWrite invokes boundary and witness.reserve; reserve validates only the witness-row budget, not managed-worktree capacity (src/runtime/workspace-witness.ts:66-79).

The shared managed_worktrees table is initialized from the supervisor witness DB, and its global count >=32 is checked only in WorktreeBindings.complete (src/runtime/worktree-bindings.ts:34-36), inside the post-ack transaction; failures roll that transaction back (src/runtime/workspace-witness.ts:107-119).

deploy/units.py:59-67,111-115 and deploy/execution_identity.py:31-36 select distinct worker/worker-root native homes but retain one supervisor home and DB. deploy/workspace_worktrees.py:79-89,264-296 checks only the selected native-home holders before physically creating the checkout and returning created:true.

.work/v230-round1-worktree-capacity-evidence.json: completedBindingsBeforeSwitch=32; reservePassed=true; completion={code:capacity,delivery:unknown}; witnessAfterCompletion.state=unknown; binding.code=worktree_unbound. The reproduction uses the actual WorkspaceWitness implementation, distinct project identities and simulated valid helper acknowledgements.

findings.title: Preserve unknown delivery when project registration fails after directory creation succeeds
findings.trigger: With 127 registered projects, start two different project/create requests before either worker result returns. Both pass the pre-await count check, both cross beforeWrite and create their directory, and both return successful worker acknowledgements. The first addProject consumes slot 128; the second addProject throws HarnessError(capacity) with its default delivery=not_sent.
findings.impact: The second operation is permanently recorded and reported as not_sent even though its directory was already created. It is absent from project/list, the user receives false safe-to-retry guidance, and no project/create positive-proof recovery path repairs this receipt. This violates the explicit not_sent versus unknown contract.
evidence: The standalone reproduction imports transformed current frozen source and uses a real in-memory SQLite Ledger, a barrier to order two positive worker acknowledgements, and actual mkdir under .work.

.work/v230-gateway-project-create-repro/proof.json: first request accepted; second request rejected with code=capacity and delivery=not_sent; second persisted receipt state=not_sent; both directoryExists=true; registeredProjects=128.

The handler catches this locally raised HarnessError through errorBody(error, unknown), but errorBody preserves the error delivery field and therefore ignores the fallback after the acknowledged side effect.
findings.relatedSameCause: The same post-success classification can be reached through object(created) or validText(created.path). Worktree receipt projection accepts identifier(worktreeId), while later Worktrees.apply calls uuid(worktreeId); malformed positive worker data there can likewise raise a default not_sent during local postprocessing. These are the same delivery-boundary defect, not separately counted findings; the concurrency case above is the dynamically confirmed trigger.
findings.recommendation: Track positive backend acknowledgement separately from dispatch and never downgrade a subsequent local postprocessing failure to not_sent. Preserve bounded recovery information and actionable guidance for a created-but-unregistered project. Optionally reserve or serialize project-registration capacity across creation/addition/worktree paths, while retaining the existing local project/rename transaction rollback exception.

limits: Complete inventory coverage with semantic review of product boundaries and structural review of generated protocol and secondary tests. Individual reports retain exact depths and limitations. Not a claim that every test was rerun or every generated line manually read. The original four findings remain recorded; subsequent repair reviews do not retroactively make this round clean.
